newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks tax credit for welfare hiring - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks tax credit for welfare hiring - NYT.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton will soon ask Congress to give tax credits to businesses that hire long-term welfare recipients, the New York Times said on Monday.
Administration officials told the paper the plan would be included in Clinton's budget next week.
The paper said the plan would let employers take a credit equal to 50 percent of the first $10,000 paid to hire people who were on welfare for at least 18 months.
The current tax credit was equal to 35 percent of the first $6,000 in wages and was paid for hiring someone on welfare for nine of the last 18 months, the paper said.
The paper said Clinton was seeking to fulfill a campaign promise to create one million jobs for welfare recipients by 2000.
